title: Stochastic capacity tiling: NA / EU / APAC GPU forecast & rollout diary
content:
Purpose:
This is a working planning sheet that explores probabilistic (stochastic) scenarios for GPU capacity by region (NA / EU / APAC), with tiling-style rollouts across sprint windows. The goal is to produce a compact operational playbook: what to provision, when to start procurement/onboarding, how large warm pools should be, and what automated triggers move us between baseline/spike/contingency lanes.

Executive summary (one paragraph):
We forecast three main demand trajectories for H1–H2 2026: Baseline growth (50% probability), Transient spike (30%) triggered by enterprise customer signings or model launches, and Persistent higher demand (20%) if new customers convert to Dedicated. Under baseline we need incremental +1.2k L4-equivalent GPUs globally by Q4 2026; spike requires +2.8k and persistent high-demand requires +3.6k. Early prioritization: NA warm pools first (60% of short-term burst), EU follow in sprint 2, APAC angled to local cloud vendor windows in sprint 3.

Assumptions (call these out explicitly):
- Workload mix: 65% short-context chat/generation, 25% embeddings, 10% batch rerank or offline fine-tune inference.
- Kernel mix and GPU equivalence: 1 H100 ~= 3 A100 v4 in throughput for our serving runtime; L4-class chips counted as 0.6 A100-equivalent.
- Target steady-state utilization target: 60% token-level utilization for hosted API; Dedicated pools expected at 75% util.
- Warm pool target: enough capacity to absorb a 2x short-term spike in request rate over 30m without adding cold instances.
- Lead times: cloud vendor contractual onboarding 3–6 business days for reserved pools; physical procurement/on-prem 8–12 weeks.

Scenario table (text matrix):
- Baseline (50%): steady growth +8% m/m traffic. Capacity add plan: NA +200 A100-eq per quarter (Q2–Q4), EU +120, APAC +80. Warm pool = 18% of active fleet.
- Spike (30%): sudden +60% traffic due to enterprise launch or seasonal regen. Capacity add plan: NA +600, EU +320, APAC +240 (one-off within 2–4 weeks). Warm pool = 30% of active fleet; active burst reserve unlocked from committed vs spot mix.
- Persistent high (20%): sustained +35% baseline. Capacity add plan: staged onboarding across 3 sprints: NA +900, EU +540, APAC +360 over 12 weeks. Warm pool 25%.

Quarterly numeric sketch (A100-equivalent GPUs) — view as planning-level knobs: (numbers are totals to add in that quarter)
- Q2 2026: NA +300, EU +160, APAC +120
- Q3 2026: NA +400, EU +240, APAC +160
- Q4 2026: NA +500, EU +300, APAC +200
(note: totals assume mixing H100/L4 procurement; final SKU mix is optimized in procurement sprint)

Rollout cadence / sprint windows (practical ops steps):
1) Sprint 0 (immediate, 0–2 weeks): validate warm-pool sizing, update autoscale policies to hold additional KV-cache slots, tag capacity candidates in cloud accounts, open vendor procurement thread.
2) Sprint 1 (2–6 weeks): Activate NA warm pool + first tranche of reserved capacity. Run soak tests with synthetic traffic (50%–200% of baseline). Confirm latency P50/P95 targets.
3) Sprint 2 (6–12 weeks): EU onboarding; enable cross-region fallback routing rules; enable model-variant fallbacks for high-cost regions.
4) Sprint 3 (12–18 weeks): APAC onboarding aligned with vendor window; ensure private deployment (VPC) setups for enterprise customers in region.

Triggers & operational thresholds (auto/manual):
- Trigger A (auto): token utilization > 70% rolling 7d AND P95 latency degradation > 15% -> spin warm-pool tranche A (NA-first).
- Trigger B (manual escalation): customer conversion Event (signed Dedicated contract) -> immediate procurement priority; plan to allocate reserved capacity within 48–72h via committed cloud reserve.
- Trigger C (contingency): cross-region failures (>=2 zones degraded) -> enable regional regional-fallback with routing quota caps; enable emergency bursting to partner pools.

Warm-pool sizing note and rationale:
- Warm pool is sized conservatively to reduce cold-start KV-cache rebuild overheads for large-context chat models. We target a minimum of 12% fleet in warm pool for baseline. Warm pool increases for spike lanes to 25–30% to avoid sustained latency SLO breaches. Warm pool vs spot: prioritize warm pool from reserved / dedicated capacity; spot used only as overflow for batch workloads.

SKU & procurement considerations (practical):
- Short-term (preferred): L4 / L4s types for high volume embeddings + cheap chat inference for non-enterprise customers; H100 reserved for large-context large-model customers.
- Vendor hedging: mix across GCP, AWS, Azure to minimize regional vendor outage risk (target 2 vendors per region where feasible).
- Cost knobs: enable quantization-friendly model variants for cheap lanes; consider CPU-offload for embeddings as cost optimization.

Utilization-led cost/benefit sketch (quick math sample):
- If baseline holds: adding 1k A100-eq at 60% util yields ~X tokens/day capacity and keeps per-token infra cost within budget profile. If utilization drops below 40% for >14 days, consider consolidation (deprovision 10% tranche) or move to spot-heavy mix.

Risk register (short bullets):
- Procurement delays (mitigation: open parallel purchase orders across vendors).
- Mis-estimated warm pool leading to cost blowout (mitigation: incremental warm-pool ramp + telemetry gating).
- Cross-region latency mismatches when routing fallbacks (mitigation: per-route SLOs and early customer opt-in for fallbacks).

Open questions / TODOs (notes to self):
- Run a 72-hour chaos test for cross-region failover before Sprint 2.
- Confirm legal timelines for multi-cloud contracts (Priya).
- Get updated cost curves from cloud-sales for L4 vs H100 across regions (Marco).
- Evaluate purchase vs commit options for EU due to localized tax/contract cadence.

Action items (owner + timeline):
- Ava: publish this sheet to infra channel and queue vendor RFIs (by 2026-03-05).
- Liam: prepare synthetic soak test config and deploy to staging warm-pool (by 2026-03-12).
- Priya: confirm contract lead times with finance and legal (by 2026-03-08).
- Marco: prepare SKU-mix optimization script and run on historical utilization traces (by 2026-03-15).

Appendix: quick telemetry slices to monitor during rollout:
- Token-level utilization (per-model, per-sku) 1m/1h/24h windows
- P50/P95 generation latency by region and model family
- Cold-start frequency and KV-cache rebuild durations by instance type
- Fraction of requests routed to fallback variants

Notes: this doc is intentionally terse and operational — meant as a live checklist for sprint planning rather than a polished report. Expect numeric values to be refined by the procurement and cost modeling sprint.
